title: Tuzi residents block traffic over COVID-19 hospitality closures
location: Tuzi, on the road between Tuzi and Podgorica, Montenegro
organizer: Tuzi residents and municipal leadership led by Mayor Nik Đeljošaj; no separate formal organizer is identified.
participants_original: Gathered Tuzi residents; no numerical estimate reported.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. RFE/RL and Anadolu describe gathered residents blocking traffic but give no turnout number or clear qualitative lower bound of 50. Search-result view/reaction totals and support from parties or visitors from Ulcinj are not protest turnout.

title.summary: Three contemporary reports describe Tuzi residents gathering and blocking the road in opposition to the additional COVID-19 measures closing local hospitality venues.

start_date.summary: Three contemporaneous reports published on 25 February describe the gathering and road block that day; Antena M dates its report to the morning. Exact onset time is not stated.

end_date.summary: RFE/RL says that late afternoon on 25 February the gathered residents withdrew, traffic normalized, and venues resumed work. This is the physical gathering end, not a policy-resolution date.

location.summary: Reports place the block on the main road in Tuzi toward Podgorica.

scope.summary: The action is reported in the municipality of Tuzi; support by political figures from Ulcinj is not coded as a second location.

organizer.summary: The reports identify local residents acting with Mayor Nik Đeljošaj and municipal leadership; no distinct formal protest group is named.

demands.summary: Residents opposed the state health authorities’ additional COVID-19 measures, including closure of local hospitality venues. The mayor’s separate discrimination/retaliation claim is attributed, not independently verified.

participants_original.summary: The reports refer to gathered residents/citizens but provide no numerical estimate.

participants_min.summary: No numeric minimum can be derived from “gathered residents” or road blockage.

participants_max.summary: None of the reports gives a maximum or count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: All three read report scopes confirm a public gathering, but none provides a count or a clearly bounded qualitative estimate of at least 50; threshold remains pending.

protester_violence.summary: The visible reports do not describe protester violence; silence does not establish its absence.

state_response.summary: Police attempted to close venues under the health order and three venue operators were arrested for health-rule violations; the report does not identify them as demonstrators. The mayor later met the deputy prime minister and health minister and said consultations would continue, but no outcome or policy concession was disclosed. Force against demonstrators remains unknown.

eligibility.summary: A public gathering and a demand concerning Montenegro’s own health restrictions are supported; attendance of at least 50 is not established.

notes: Antena M describes the morning road block; RFE/RL reports that residents withdrew and traffic normalized in the late afternoon on 25 February, supporting the physical end date. Government dialogue is coded as accommodation because officials met the municipal leader to discuss the measure; this does not imply a policy concession. The mayor attributed the local restrictions to retaliation over Kosovo-independence celebrations and Albanian flags; that allegation remains attributed and unresolved. Website views, venue/workforce counts, police presence, Ulcinj visitors, and party support are not turnout.
open_questions: Did at least 50 people attend the Tuzi gathering?
Were any demonstrators arrested, beaten, or forcibly dispersed, or were there injuries? The three reported arrests concern venue operators and are not established as arrests of protesters.
Did the government meeting produce any change to the local health measures, and what demands were formally considered?
Was the mayor’s discrimination/retaliation allegation supported by independent evidence?
Do any other contemporaneous reports provide a numerical crowd estimate?
